title: `MOD` of doubles: truncated, but NaN for an infinite divisor
verdict: `MOD(x, inf)` is NaN, C's fmod gives x; zero raises; sverify writes the cases
description: `MOD(5.5, 2)` is 1.5 and `MOD(-5.5, 2)` -1.5: the dividend's sign, as C's `fmod`. A zero divisor raises. `MOD(inf, 2)` and `MOD(NaN, 2)` are NaN, but `MOD(5.5, inf)` is NaN too, where `fmod` gives 5.5.
reference: `modulus` of doubles is `fmod`. sverify's SQL (`Dialect.float_mod`) writes the edge cases out, so only finite operands reach `MOD`; `writer-float-mod` gives 5.5 for `(5.5, inf)`.

provenance.checked_by: sverify_dev.probe_snowflake through the Snowflake CLI (Snowflake characterization session)

evidence.sql: SELECT a, b, mod(a, b), a % b FROM (VALUES (5.5::FLOAT, 2::FLOAT), (-5.5::FLOAT, 2::FLOAT), (5.5::FLOAT, -2::FLOAT), ('inf'::FLOAT, 2::FLOAT), (5.5::FLOAT, 'inf'::FLOAT), ('NaN'::FLOAT, 2::FLOAT)) AS s(a, b)

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_snowflake` runs each query through `snow sql` (Snowflake CLI 3.32.1) on an X-Small warehouse, Snowflake 10.40.102, with the session's `TIMEZONE` set to UTC and `USE_CACHED_RESULT` off; every other parameter is the account's default, recorded in the header of probes.json (`WEEK_START` 0, `WEEK_OF_YEAR_POLICY` 0, `DEFAULT_NULL_ORDERING` LAST, `TIMESTAMP_TYPE_MAPPING` TIMESTAMP_NTZ). The inputs are literal `VALUES`, except the `sample-*` probes, which read TPC-H's LINEITEM (6,001,215 rows) in SNOWFLAKE_SAMPLE_DATA.
